title: Supreme Court Declines Urgent Curb on CJP Tiranga March as Police Offer 11-Person Event
excerpt: The court hoped better sense would prevail and listed the Central Park closure plea for October 26-27, while Delhi Police urged the public to stay away and traders warned of festive-season losses.
body:
• The Supreme Court on Friday declined an urgent order on the CJP 'Lehra Do Tiranga' gathering in Connaught Place, saying it hoped better sense would prevail, and listed the plea for October 26 or 27.
  • Delhi Police have urged the public to stay away from Central Park and offered to facilitate a symbolic flag-waving event for a select group of 11 people at a suitable place instead.
  • Central Park stays shut on October 16 and 17, with prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS in force across Connaught Place and adjoining areas.
  • Traders and vendors say a protest-related closure in the festive season threatens daily livelihoods; protesters say the march defends the right to demonstrate after two CJP leaders were jailed.

Court declines urgent intervention

The Supreme Court on Friday refused to issue urgent directions over the Cockroach Janta Party's proposed 'Lehra Do Tiranga' gathering at Central Park in Connaught Place, while flagging the cost to small businesses if the area is shut down. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi was hearing a plea against the New Delhi Municipal Council's decision to close Central Park on October 16 and 17.

https://x.com/rishikeshlaw/status/2110682286677229701

"We hope better sense will prevail on everyone."

— Supreme Court bench, as reported in coverage of the hearing

The bench noted that small shopkeepers depend on festive-season earnings and that protest rights, law and order, and livelihoods are connected questions. It indicated the court could use its constitutional powers if business losses followed, and listed the matter for October 26 or 27, according to reports of the proceedings summarised by Kashmir InFocus. The refusal of an urgent hearing is not permission for a mass march: existing prohibitory orders remain in force and police remain responsible for regulating any gathering.

The protesters' position

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke called supporters to gather at Central Park at 5 p.m. with the national flag after co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody in Tihar Jail. The party says the two were jailed for unfurling the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar after that site was denotified for protests, and frames the march as a defence of democratic rights and as part of its wider campaign over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and its demand for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

On Thursday, the Delhi High Court had also refused to restrain Dipke and the CJP from holding the protest, while recording the police assurance that all possible steps would be taken to regulate it under the law, PTI reported via the Nagaland Post. Protest supporters argue that successive restrictions — the denotification of Jantar Mantar, the park closure and the 11-person limit — leave no practical space for a visible demonstration in central Delhi.

The police, traders and government concerns

Delhi Police say the march has not been granted permission for a mass gathering. They have appealed to the public not to assemble at Central Park, cited Section 163 orders in Connaught Place and adjoining areas, and offered a narrower alternative: a select group of 11 people carrying the national flag and singing the national anthem at a suitable location, with the flag handled with prescribed respect and decorum. Police and the NDMC say Central Park, above Rajiv Chowk Metro station, will remain closed for administrative reasons on both days, and security has been tightened across the commercial district.

Traders and vendors brought the other half of the case to court. A Connaught Place vendor's plea argued that Connaught Place is not a designated protest site and that losing another festive weekend to closures would put traders and street vendors on the street, in their counsel's words. Market associations have sought protection for shops during the festive season, when daily sales support entire families — a concern the Supreme Court bench explicitly acknowledged. The government side, through the Additional Solicitor General in the High Court, assured judges that steps had already been taken to control and regulate the CJP's activity and that the petitioners' apprehensions would be taken care of.

What happens next

The immediate question is whether the 5 p.m. call produces the limited 11-person symbolic event the police have offered, a larger gathering the police must disperse, or a change of plan by the organisers. Live coverage tracked by Jagran reported heavy deployment around Rajiv Chowk, Central Park, nearby metro stations and Palika Bazar, with Central Park shut and traffic advisories in place. The Supreme Court plea returns on October 26 or 27, and the High Court matter is listed for November 3 — meaning the legal argument over protest space, festive trade and police regulation in central Delhi will continue well after Friday's gathering.
